gaps.sentence: They made me ___ for the whole team's mistake.
gaps.explanation: make + object + bare infinitive in active sentences: made me apologise.

gaps.sentence: They agreed ___ the deadline by a week.
gaps.explanation: 'Agree to do something' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: He apologized for ___ so abrupt in the meeting.
I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: Despite ___ three times, he didn't give up.
We're looking forward to ___ from you soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Look forward to + -ing' — 'to' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.
would rather takes the bare infinitive: I'd rather stay.

gaps.sentence: The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).
